description: A bar chart that compares each month against the one before answers "is this month better than the last one". It does not answer the question the meeting is actually about: are we on plan. Bar Chart with Variation % answers both. It writes the variance % between bars by itself, and it draws a marker where each bar should have been — your plan, your budget, your forecast or last year. No DATEADD, no variance column, no helper measures. PLAN VS ACTUAL • A reference marker on every bar: bind Plan / Budget, Forecast or Previous Year and pick it under Compare to • The variance on every bar, as %, as a difference in the units of your measure, or both • Bars below plan take the negative colour; a connector joins each label to its bar through the marker • Against the previous bar: the variance % between consecutive bars, with arrows and brackets • Analytical lines — average, maximum, minimum, median, a reference value and a trend line — and a reference band that marks the typical range of your data SMALL MULTIPLES • One panel per region, product or team, on a shared scale so the panels are actually comparable • Choose the number of columns, or leave it automatic; minimum panel size with scroll • Vertical columns or horizontal bars LOOKS RIGHT FROM THE FIRST CLICK • Colours from your report theme; six style templates, including an IBCS style • A setup guide in the corner while you…
